desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Fujian Provincial Hospital; conditions: Critical Illness, Traumatic Brain Injury, Subarachnoid Hemorrhage, Intracerebral Hemorrhage, Intracranial Hypertension; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 100; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Mortality prediction in neurocritical care relies on scores computed at admission, which cannot update as the clinical course evolves. We previously developed a landmark-based machine learning model that converts hourly physiological data, including intracranial pressure, into an updating risk of death. The model was developed in a large public database and validated retrospectively in a second, independent one. This prospective multicentre study will test the model in consecutive patients at participating hospitals in Fujian Province, China. Physiological data will be collected as part of routine care. The model will generate risk estimates that are recorded for analysis but not shown to treating clinicians, and no treatment decision will be influenced by the study. The primary analysis will assess discrimination and calibration of the model for death during the intensive care stay. Secondary analyses will compare the model with severity scores in routine use and examine performance by aetiology.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Aesthetic Surgery.
desc: [Clinics in plastic surgery] This article surveys artificial intelligence (AI) applications across aesthetic plastic surgery, spanning large language models (publicly available software, practice chatbots, and clinical decision support tools), simulation technologies (3 dimensional imaging platforms like Vectra and Crisalix, generative adversarial network-based and diffusion-based image generation), surgical planning, and operational tools for documentation, billing, scheduling, and marketing. It highlights validation evidence where available, alongside persistent limitations including training data bias, hallucinations, black-box opacity, and unresolved regulatory and liability questions. Despite AI's expanding capabilities, individualized surgical judgment remains irreplaceable, positioning AI as a decision-support tool that enhances, rather than substitutes, the surgeon-patient relationship.

title: Impact of Pretraining Length, Model Size, and Annotation Budget on Downstream Clinical Tasks of Foundation Models in Radiotherapy
desc: Cone-beam CT (CBCT) scans acquired during radiotherapy capture changes such as tumor shrinkage and radiation-induced tissue changes, offering great potential for foundation models that help monitor individual treatment responses. However, to our knowledge, no large-scale pretrained models for radiotherapy CBCT exist, and evaluating modeling choices is difficult since downstream tasks are not known in advance. We examine how pretraining length, model size, and finetuning strategy relate to downstream clinical performance, and how metrics tracked during pretraining correlate with it. We pretrain vision transformer encoders with masked image modeling on about 150,000 raw 3D radiotherapy CBCT scans, tracking representation quality via validation loss, effective rank, and linear probing. Downstream tasks are classification of feeding tube presence ($n=51,135$ CBCTs, $1,562$ patients) and clinical characteristics (T-, N-stage, sex, age, tumor site; $n=1,278$ patients) in head and neck cancer. We compare low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and full finetuning against no pretraining, varying annotated dataset size. Pretext validation loss was the most consistent predictor of downstream performance; effective rank and linear probing were also associated, but not consistently across model sizes and finetuning methods. LoRA performed comparably to full finetuning while training only 0.5-2.5% of the parameters. Fully finetuned models consistently outperformed models without pretraining across all sizes, with AUROC 0.91-0.97 vs. 0.58-0.85 for feeding tube classification and 0.99-1.00 vs. 0.71-0.97 for sex classification. Model size had only a small, inconsistent effect, suggesting smaller models suffice at lower computational cost. Code and pretrained models (non-commercial license): https://github.com/alexCortinaU/RT-CBCT_SSL

title: Sequence-based models predict TF binding with negligible contributions from motif cooperativity
desc: How transcription factors (TFs) selectively recognize their genomic targets among numerous sites containing similar DNA motifs remains an open question. Cooperative binding at neighboring motif sites is widely considered a key mechanism of TF specificity, yet its genome-wide contribution remains unclear. Machine learning models can now predict TF binding directly from DNA sequence, providing opportunities to investigate its underlying determinants. Here, we leveraged BPNet models trained on ~2,000 ENCODE TF binding profiles to systematically assess motif cooperativity. Although detected at individual loci, cooperativity made a negligible contribution to genome-wide binding predictions. Nevertheless, the models captured differences in binding preferences between TFs with similar motif preferences, even within the same cellular environment. These findings highlight the need to critically assess prevailing assumptions and explore alternative mechanisms underlying selective TF binding.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Surgical Education.
desc: [Clinics in plastic surgery] Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly transformed education, including plastic surgical training through adaptive learning platforms, automated competency assessment and intraoperative performance analytics. These platforms support competency-based medical education by enabling continuous objective evaluation, personalized feedback, trajectory predictions, and scalable simulation environments. Emerging applications include virtual patients, plastic surgery-specific adaptive question banks, surgical video analysis, and augmented-reality operative guidance. Despite promising gains in efficiency and educational precision, implementation will require careful validation, transparency, and sustained expert oversight. Strategic AI integration into training programs offers the potential to enhance technical skill acquisition, standardize evaluation and expand access to high-quality surgical education globally.

title: Efficient Self-Supervised Adaptation of 3D Abdominal Vision-Language Model for Institution-Specific HCC Classification via Full Fine-Tuning and PEFT
desc: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) capture cross-modal relationships between image and text, yet their adaptation to institution-specific clinical tasks remains underexplored. In this study, we fine-tuned a pretrained 3D medical VLM for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) classification using paired abdominal CT scans and radiology reports from a different institution with acquisition characteristics that differ from the model's original pretraining corpus. We compared two adaptation strategies: full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), motivated by the common use of PEFT to reduce computational cost and enable adaptation under limited-data constraints. Both approaches achieve strong downstream HCC classification performance despite the cross-institutional domain shift, with PEFT reaching an AUC of 0.79 and F1 of 0.70, and full fine-tuning achieving an AUC of 0.82 and F1 of 0.71. Although these results remain below the performance reported by supervised HCC classification approaches, our method achieves improvements over the pretrained model through CT-report contrastive learning without requiring lesion-level annotations or HCC classification labels as training targets. Full fine-tuning converges rapidly but overfits within a few epochs, whereas PEFT (ConvLoRA for the image encoder and LoRA for the text encoder) attains comparable performance while updating approximately 1% of the model parameters, although requiring more training steps. We also examine the role of contrastive temperature, observing that temperature initialization significantly affects classification performance. This study demonstrates that a 3D medical VLM can be efficiently adapted to institution-specific HCC classification using self-supervised CT-report contrastive learning, while highlighting the practical trade-offs between full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Antibiotic Resistance Genes: Performance, Interpretability, and Cross-Database Redundancy
desc: Antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) classifiers are typically developed and evaluated within a single curated database, leaving open how much two independently curated databases agree and what that implies for apparent cross-database generalization. We trained an XGBoost classifier on amino acid trigram frequencies and physicochemical descriptors using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD), the field's largest curated ARG resource. The model separated resistance genes from non-resistance proteins with near-ceiling accuracy (AUROC = 0.982, MCC = 0.886); a label-shuffling null baseline collapsed to chance (AUROC = 0.508) and bootstrap confidence intervals were narrow, confirming genuine signal rather than data leakage or overfitting. SHAP analysis attributed this performance to biologically interpretable features, notably the trigram KTG, isoelectric point, and aromaticity, each consistent with known catalytic motifs in resistance enzymes. Before testing the classifier against ResFinder, one of CARD's most widely used counterparts, we assessed database independence by clustering sequences with CD-HIT, finding that 96.8-98.7% of ResFinder sequences shared substantial protein identity with CARD even at a permissive 50% identity threshold, indicating the two databases largely represent the same sequence population, with direct implications for how cross-database generalization should be measured. On the small subset of ResFinder sequences genuinely non-redundant with CARD (40-100 sequences, depending on threshold), the classifier failed completely, never classifying any as resistance genes; SHAP traced this failure to sequence length, as non-redundant sequences are nearly three times longer than training proteins, and length is among the model's most influential features. The same pattern emerged by resistance mechanism: the model achieved perfect accuracy on beta-lactamases, compact single-domain enzymes well represented in training (100%, n = 351), but correctly identified only 38.5% of efflux pump components (n = 13), a mechanism built from large, multi-domain transporters rather than compact catalytic enzymes. Together, these results describe a capable, interpretable ARG classifier alongside a quantified methodological caution: cross-database redundancy must be measured rather than assumed, and when a sequence-composition classifier fails, the failure is often explained by protein architecture rather than database origin.

Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence-based Monitoring Technique for Measuring Oral Hygiene during Orthodontic Therapy.
desc: [Annals of African medicine] Good oral hygiene is mandatory for orthodontic patients. This study was done for evaluating how well an artificial intelligence (AI)-based supervising system could improve oral hygiene during orthodontic procedures. A total of 44 patients who were undergoing for permanent orthodontic procedures were split into two groups of 22 each: Group I as the control, and Group II as the AI monitoring test group. The test group's patients were instructed to get routine intraoral scans using Scanbox (Dental Monitoring®). For all groups, the Orthodontic Plaque Index and Marginal Gingival Index (MGI) were measured at baseline (T0), 2 weeks later (T1, T2, and T3, respectively), and at 3 months (T4). A statistical analysis was performed on the collected data. Subjects in the test group showed a considerable decrease in gingival inflammation and plaque score in contrast to the control group. Plaque and gingival irritation are reduced during orthodontic treatment when a remote monitoring system is used. By using this technique, patients are able to maintain the greatest possible dental health.

title: Where Does Hindsight Enter Clinical Agent Benchmarks? An Audit of Simulators and Case Construction
desc: Benchmarks for LLM diagnostic agents are built from retrospective records: the case an agent reads is rewritten from discharge summaries, and unrecorded test results are generated by a simulator that often sees the final diagnosis. HindAudit separates three hindsight channels (the diagnosis given to the simulator, the retrospective context it conditions on, and the agent-facing case text) and measures each with judges trained only on real data. On 27,489 emergency admissions from MIMIC-IV, five registered tests found no leakage into simulated laboratory results: providing the diagnosis to five simulators had a negligible effect, and prompted gatekeepers diluted the diagnostic signal, although exploratory results suggest they can raise agent scores. The largest effect lay in the case text. Against a presentation-time reconstruction from triage records, benchmark-style summaries raised the zero-shot accuracy of four LLMs from 25.4% to 39.7% and discharge histories to 45.3%, and raised six interactive agents' scores while barely changing their ranking. The exploratory gap was reproduced in a registered replication on held-out patients. Masking diagnosis names left it unchanged. Because MIMIC lacks a contemporaneous bedside history, the gap is an upper bound on hindsight. We report all registered outcomes and recommend construction practices.

title: Pharmacophore-Inspired Virtual Receptor: Generating Realistic Peptide Binding Data for Machine Learning
desc: VReceptor is a virtual receptor simulation framework that generates realistic, sequence-dependent binding data for peptide-based therapeutics. It combines pharmacophore-inspired weighting schemes with amino acid similarity metrics to evaluate peptide design strategies in a controlled environment. Validation using the Prolactin-Releasing Peptide (PrRP) dataset confirms VReceptor's ability to approximate binding behaviours and optimize experimental planning. This framework empowers researchers in computational peptide design and active learning workflows while highlighting areas for further refinement.

From static structures to conformational ensembles: Artificial intelligence for protein sampling and dynamics.
source: PubMed · Current opinion in structural biology
desc: [Current opinion in structural biology] After sparking a revolution in protein structure prediction, machine learning (ML), and artificial intelligence (AI) are now reshaping the modeling of protein conformational ensembles and dynamics. A fast, scalable, and accurate representation of protein conformational ensembles could enable genome-scale studies of protein function, with broad applications in drug discovery and protein engineering. The challenges associated with this goal, however, are far greater than those involved in single structure prediction because of the broad timescales spanned by protein motion, the complex relationship between sequence and dynamics, and the scarcity of datasets with experimental measurements. Despite these difficulties, many promising solutions have emerged in recent years, ranging from accelerated molecular dynamics to direct sampling of the conformational distribution, as well as some hybrid methods. Here, we review recent AI-powered approaches to tackle protein dynamics and conformational sampling, and outline their current limitations.

title: Unsupervised Multi-modal Medical Image Registration via Invertible Translation
desc: In medical imaging, the alignment of multi-modal images plays a critical role in providing comprehensive information for image-guided therapies. Despite its importance, multi-modal image registration poses significant challenges due to the complex and often unknown spatial relationships between different image modalities. To address this, we introduce a novel unsupervised translation-based multi-modal registration method, termed Invertible Neural Network-based Registration (INNReg). INNReg consists of an image-to-image translation network that converts multi-modal images into mono-modal counterparts and a registration network that uses the translated mono-modal images to align the multi-modal images. Specifically, to ensure the preservation of geometric consistency after image translation, we introduce an Invertible Neural Network (INN) that leverages a dynamic depthwise convolution-based local attention mechanism. Additionally, we design a novel barrier loss function based on Normalized Mutual Information to impose constraints on the registration network, which enhances the registration accuracy. The superior performance of INNReg is demonstrated through experiments on two public multi-modal medical image datasets, including MRI T1/T2 and MRI/CT pairs. The code is available at https://github.com/MeggieGuo/INNReg

title: Casanovo-TMT: deep learning-based de novo sequencing of TMTpro-labeled peptides and phosphopeptides
desc: De novo peptide sequencing reads peptides directly from tandem mass spectra, but none of the released deep learning models can sequence peptides labeled with isobaric tags such as TMTpro, which are widely used for multiplexed quantitative proteomics. We extended the residue vocabulary of Casanovo with TMTpro tags and phosphorylation, fine-tuned it on 21 million spectra from our laboratory, most of them TMTpro-labeled, and re-ranked the candidates in the beam by their agreement with the measured precursor mass. The resulting model, Casanovo-TMT, predicted the exact peptidoform for 84.7% of the TMTpro-labeled spectra in our test set and for 87.4 and 79.6% of the spectra in two public global-proteome datasets from other laboratories, whereas the extended vocabulary without fine-tuning gave 0.3%. Discarding the lowest-scoring predictions raised precision to 95% while retaining 81.7% of the test spectra. Casanovo-TMT also predicted the exact peptidoform for 69.2% of the spectra in a public phosphopeptide-enriched dataset and for 66 to 72% of the phosphopeptide spectra in three phosphoproteomic studies from our laboratory that were not used for training. In these studies, it identified numbers of phosphopeptides comparable to or larger than those of database search engines, and proportionally more where database search identified fewer. For the phosphopeptides identified only by Casanovo-TMT, entrapment estimated that more than 90% were correct, and an independent search engine assigned the same sequence to 95 to 98% of the spectra that it identified with confidence. Casanovo-TMT can therefore extend database search in TMTpro-based quantitative proteomics, particularly in studies in which database search identifies few phosphopeptides.

Artificial intelligence-based finish-line detection and margin-related accuracy in fixed prosthodontic digital workflows: A systematic review and functional meta-synthesis.
source: PubMed · The Journal of prosthetic dentistry
desc: [The Journal of prosthetic dentistry] Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly incorporated into fixed prosthodontic digital workflows, but evidence regarding finish-line detection, margin handling, and margin-related crown accuracy remains heterogeneous. The purpose of this systematic review was to evaluate AI-based finish-line detection, margin-line extraction, and margin-related accuracy in tooth-supported fixed prosthodontic workflows using a functional meta-synthesis. The PubMed, Scopus, and Embase databases were searched through May 2026. Studies evaluating AI, machine learning, or deep learning for finish-line detection, margin extraction, crown design, margin-aware crown generation, or margin-related accuracy were included. Findings were synthesized according to the functional role of AI, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using an adapted quality framework. A total of 17 studies were included. AI demonstrated measurable performance for margin detection and supported crown-design workflows, frequently reducing design time. Marginal and internal adaptation were generally clinically acceptable or comparable with conventional workflows, although superiority was inconsistent. Quantitative pooling was precluded by substantial methodological and outcome heterogeneity. AI showed technical feasibility for margin-sensitive fixed prosthodontic workflows, but current evidence remains heterogeneous, predominantly early-stage, and insufficient to establish consistent clinical superiority.

title: Beyond Acuity Accuracy: A Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Emergency Triage AI Tools
desc: Patient-facing AI triage tools may support care-seeking and emergency department prioritization, but require evaluation beyond acuity accuracy alone. We developed SAFE-Triage, a framework integrating human review, automated metrics, LLM-as-judge evaluation, and simulation testing across clinical performance, patient interaction, and clinician-facing summary quality. We applied SAFE-Triage to 40 MIMIC-IV-derived emergency vignettes and a 10,030-case acuity analysis comparing prompted LLM triage (PLT) with rule-augmented prompted LLM triage (rPLT). PLT achieved higher emergency severity index (ESI) accuracy (57.5% vs 42.8%, $P < 0.001$), lower undertriage (13.1% vs 29.8%, $P < 0.001$), and higher clinician ratings across all domains. rPLT produced shorter and more stable outputs with higher automated readability scores. SAFE-Triage identified trade-offs between acuity accuracy, undertriage risk, communication quality, readability, and summary quality, supporting pre-deployment refinement and ongoing monitoring by showing where triage tools are efficient, need improvement, or need clinician oversight.

Artificial intelligence-enabled healthcare access and user experience: comparative institutional analysis and survey evidence from China.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] Regulatory entry and public experience describe different aspects of artificial intelligence-enabled healthcare access. This health policy study compares institutional arrangements in China, the United States, and the European Union, examines the coverage of equity-related evidence, and analyses an online Chinese survey. Of 480 submissions, 430 passed an attention check, including 32 respondents without reported functional contact and 398 entering the experience models. The institutional comparison identifies differences in regulatory objects, information recipients, and responsibility allocation. The coverage analysis distinguishes institutional information and hospital governance from measured portal use and service experience. In the survey, lower-capability respondents reported greater entry and operational barriers; 79 of 159 reported reducing or abandoning use because of barriers. Among contacted respondents, functional contact intensity was positively associated with perceived process ease (standardized β = 0.496), which was associated with perceived health-service responsiveness (standardized β = 0.381). The contact-by-capability interaction was negative (B = -0.254), contrary to the hypothesized direction. The findings highlight entry and operational barriers alongside differences in experience among existing users, supporting evaluation of both access conditions and service encounters.

title: SCAN: Site-Aware Collaborative Privacy-Preserving Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Neurological Disease Classification
desc: Worldwide neuroimaging data could strengthen diagnostic foundation models, but privacy rules often prevent centralizing brain MRI scans. We present SCAN, a site-aware collaborative adaptation framework for Neurological Disease Classification that lets new sites adapt a 3D medical vision-language model (VLM) without retraining or sharing patient scans. Each site keeps exact class prototypes for local prediction and can share privacy-protected class summaries: norm-bounded sums and counts perturbed once with calibrated noise. Using 7,641 scans from 67 sites across 12 countries, covering Alzheimer's disease (AD), stroke, epilepsy and controls, we assess local adaptation, cross-site benefits, and effects on existing sites. At seven unseen sites, the frozen VLM's zero-shot AUCs were 0.833-0.945 for AD and stroke. Training-free local prototypes improved epilepsy AUC at three sites from 0.598/0.625/0.508 to 0.684/0.729/0.762 and AD AUC at one site from 0.833 to 0.863, nearly matching a classifier trained at each site (mean AUC 0.757 vs. 0.759). With differential privacy ($ε$ = 4), new sites contributed without materially reducing accuracy at existing sites (AUC change $\leq$0.2%), although gains from sharing were limited, and membership attacks performed near chance. SCAN offers hospitals a worldwide framework to adapt and share brain MRI VLMs without exchanging scans or retraining.

Generative Artificial Intelligence-Based Dietary Advice: A Scoping Review of Nutritional Accuracy, Safety, and Eating-Related Risks.
desc: [Clinical nutrition ESPEN] This scoping review aimed to synthesize current evidence on generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based dietary advice, with particular attention to nutritional accuracy, safety, weight-management guidance, eating-related harm, and professional safeguards. A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework, refined by Levac et al., and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Embase were searched up to 30 June 2026. Original empirical studies evaluating generative AI or large language models for dietary advice, meal planning, nutritional information, weight management, or eating-disorder-related guidance were eligible. Study selection, data charting, and synthesis were performed independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus or third-reviewer assessment. Nine studies published between 2023 and 2026 were included. In this small and emerging evidence base, one study reported 84.38% accuracy on an objective nutrition-literacy assessment, and another found overall Diet Quality Index-International scores above 70 for chatbot-generated weight-loss plans. However, important limitations were identified in caloric accuracy, portion sizing, macronutrient and micronutrient balance, reproducibility, personalization, and management of food allergies and multimorbidity. Potential safety concerns were identified in adolescent and eating-disorder scenarios, where chatbot responses sometimes combined appropriate healthy-eating advice with restrictive or weight-focused recommendations; these studies did not establish resulting clinical or behavioral harm. Although some systems encouraged consultation with healthcare professionals, safety warnings and referral to regulated resources were inconsistent. Evidence from the nine included studies remains preliminary, heterogeneous, and largely simulation-based. Generative AI may have a supplementary role in nutrition education and preliminary dietary guidance, but the available evidence is insufficient to support autonomous use in place of dietitians. Current findings indicate potential safety risks in high-risk or clinically complex scenarios rather than demonstrated long-term harm. Longitudinal and real-world studies are needed to establish the clinical and behavioral effects of AI-generated dietary advice.

title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
desc: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities. For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction. With InclusionMed-DxFiles, our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells. We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the InclusionMed Index, with overall scores ranging from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100. The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, showing that a model's rank varied with the role or capability considered. A within-benchmark analysis using task-level tags showed that the ten highest-ranked models in the Index all scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making. Models with similar Index scores also differed substantially in estimated inference cost. These findings highlight the need for evaluation covering more diverse healthcare needs and for context-specific model selection. Through open collaboration and community contributions, InclusionMed seeks to ensure that diverse healthcare needs worldwide shape how medical AI progress is defined and measured.

Artificial Intelligence and Leadership in Academic Plastic Surgery.
desc: [Clinics in plastic surgery] Artificial intelligence (AI) offers surgical leaders a means of augmenting-not replacing-the craft of leadership. This article outlines practical applications across strategic vision, such as innovation and problem-solving, recruitment and faculty development, meetings and decision-making, project execution, academic productivity, and regulatory governance, while delineating where AI reliably fails: judgment, accountability, and contextual nuance. It introduces the throughput asymmetry that arises when AI-accelerated leaders outpace an unequipped implementing organization, and addresses the heterogeneous AI exposure spanning AI-native trainees and appropriately skeptical senior faculty. Governance should be constructed as an iterative loop rather than a static policy.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
desc: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators. Automated correction of the residual structural errors is currently addressed one anatomy at a time, so the number of trained correctors scales with the number of segmentation targets. We present GRACE, a retrieval-augmented refiner that edits an input mask under context drawn from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases. The refiner is trained once on a multi-organ corpus spanning compact organs, cavities, branching vessels, and tumour lesions. In the held-out dataset-transfer evaluation, three held-out datasets query a fixed knowledge base built from training data only. A separate leave-one-anatomy-out experiment tests parameter-free index extension: verified cases of an unseen solid organ enter the knowledge base, and the refiner stays frozen. A light shape-aware projection head on a frozen multimodal encoder maps embedding similarity to the shape agreement of the masks, so the knowledge base returns cases that the refiner can use as a shape prior. We evaluate GRACE on 18 public datasets spanning CT, MRI and ultrasound, using nine refinement configurations and seven upstream segmentors that span weak, mid, and strong operating regimes. We report each change with the DSC of its input mask. On the weak tier, the input DSC is 0.386 and GRACE adds up to +0.35 DSC. On a strong segmentor, the input DSC is 0.932 and the mean change is small. Transfer to an imaging modality that is absent from training and from the index is partial and depends on the anatomy, and remains an open research direction. Our results suggest retrieval-conditioned refinement is a practical alternative to anatomy-specific correction models. Code: https://github.com/robustml-eurecom/grace

title: Sofinnova books biggest-ever $815M fund with an eye toward up-and-coming ‘global leaders’
WHITE-Net: White matter HyperIntensities Tissue Extraction using deep learning network.
desc: [Imaging neuroscience (Cambridge, Mass.)] White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are a hallmark of cerebral small vessel disease, a highly prevalent condition in aging, making their accurate detection in large-scale magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies critically important. Currently available semi-automated and automated segmentation methods are frequently limited by sensitivity to variations in imaging conditions and computational constraints, restricting their applicability across diverse acquisition settings. We present WHITE-Net, a deep learning-based framework for automated WMH segmentation built on a 3D ResUNet architecture and trained on multisite MRI data encompassing substantial variability in scanner vendors, acquisition protocols, spatial resolution, and image characteristics. Evaluated across three independent datasets-BrainLaus, ADNI, and WMH Challenge, WHITE-Net achieves high segmentation accuracy and ranks among the top-performing methods across datasets, enabling a comprehensive assessment of generalizability in varied imaging environments. WHITE-Net maintains stable performance in a wide spectrum of lesion loads and demonstrates a favorable balance between precision and recall, effectively limiting false positive detections-a common limitation of existing approaches. Beyond accuracy, WHITE-Net requires no parameter tuning and offers fast inference times, making it well suited for deployment in large-scale neuroimaging studies. The obtained results highlight the value of training on diverse multisite data for improving generalizability and position WHITE-Net as a reliable, scalable tool for automated WMH segmentation in computational anatomy research.

title: Optimising Recruitment and Sample Allocation in Multi-Site Rare Disease Studies
desc: Clinical research in rare diseases is challenged by the limited availability and broad geographical distribution of eligible patients. This necessitates multi-centre collaboration and strategic selection of analytical laboratories based on capacity, cost, and capability. We present a mathematical framework based on cardinality optimisation to support key operational decisions in study design, balancing clinical relevance, feasibility, budgetary constraints, and logistical factors. The framework was implemented in the Reconstruction and Computational Modelling for Inherited Metabolic Diseases (Recon4IMD) project, aiming to recruit 1,900 diagnosed patients across 24 healthcare centres and eight metabolomic laboratories. Compared to both proportional heuristic and greedy marginal allocation baselines, the proposed optimisation model consistently achieved higher recruitment yields in simulated multi-centre scenarios and reduced metabolomic analysis costs by approximately 30% under unconstrained conditions. Notably, both the heuristic and greedy allocation baselines became infeasible under progressively tighter laboratory capacity constraints, whereas the optimised model maintained feasibility and cost control. These findings highlight the value of integrated optimisation strategies for improving recruitment, platform selection, and sample allocation in complex, resource-limited research settings.

title: Helus' chemically modified psychedelic hits key goals in phase 3 depression trial
Artificial Intelligence in Acute Stroke: Applications and Implications for the Portuguese National Healthcare System.
desc: [Acta medica portuguesa] Acute stroke is a leading cause of death and long-term disability in Portugal. Rapid and accurate imaging is critical to guide acute stroke management, and artificial intelligence has shown growing potential to support triage, quantification, and therapeutic decision-making. This study aimed to characterize the current use of artificial intelligence in acute stroke imaging workflow in Portuguese public hospital neuroradiology departments, and to identify perceived benefits, implementation barriers and prospects. A descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted using an online questionnaire distributed between January and April 2026 to neuroradiology departments of Portuguese public hospitals with stroke intervention units. The questionnaire covered department characterization, current use of artificial intelligence, and perceptions regarding future applications. Responses were analyzed descriptively. Ten hospitals from the North, Centre, Lisbon Metropolitan Area, South and insular regions were included. All operated under a stroke code protocol, used computed tomography as the first-line modality, and provided 24-hour neuroradiology coverage through a combined on-site and teleradiology model. Only two hospitals used dedicated artificial intelligence software, and one was in an implementation phase. Three additional centers used computational tools with artificial intelligence functionalities without identifying them as such. Prior contact with artificial intelligence was reported by 80% of respondents, and all anticipated its integration into routine practice. The most frequently cited applications were automated ASPECTS, core/penumbra quantification, large vessel occlusion identification and hemorrhage detection. Faster time-to-treatment and support for teleradiology workflows were the most perceived benefits. Opinions on funding were divided between the hospital institution and the state. Formal staff training was reported only by one center. Despite high awareness and a well-established organizational framework, adoption of artificial intelligence remains limited. Coordinated procurement strategies, structured training programs and shared operational definitions of artificial intelligence are needed to enable broader and more equitable integration into stroke care.

title: Who Pays for Byzantine Robustness? Validity, Data-Share Dictatorships, and Fairness When Only a Few Hospitals Collaborate
desc: Clinical federated learning (FL) collaborations typically connect only three to six hospitals, yet Byzantine-robust aggregation rules are designed and benchmarked on synthetic partitions across dozens of equal-sized clients. We conduct an empirical audit of eight standard aggregation rules: FedAvg, coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, Krum, Multi-Krum, Bulyan, geometric median (GeoMed), and Centered Clipping (CC). We evaluate both unweighted and sample-size-weighted variants across three cross-silo medical datasets from the FLamby benchmark: Fed-Heart-Disease ($n = 4$ hospitals), Fed-TCGA-BRCA ($n = 6$ regions), and Fed-ISIC2019 ($n = 6$ centres). We execute 54,214 training runs across enumerated attacker coalitions ($f \in \{1, 2\}$) paired with exact-twin leave-out controls that decompose performance drops into honest data loss versus adversarial attack damage. We report three findings. First, client-count validity checks fail to capture breakdown in skewed medical consortia: while $n = 6, f = 1$ satisfies every count condition except Bulyan's, assigning sample-size weights turns median and GeoMed into a clean-model dictatorship whenever a single hospital holds more than half the training data, and causes weighted median, GeoMed, and CC to collapse when that dominant centre attacks. Second, exact-twin leave-out controls reveal that when the largest hospital attacks, the apparent failure of count-based robust rules is predominantly caused by the loss of honest training data (7.5 to 10.4 points on ISIC) rather than adversarial perturbation (2.3 to 3.8 points on ISIC). Conversely, weight-dependent rules suffer large true attack damage (16.1 to 25.1 points on ISIC). Third, unweighted robust rules consistently discount whichever institution generates the most atypical parameter updates, penalizing the smallest hospital on Heart but penalizing larger institutions on TCGA and ISIC.

title: FDA’s complete response letter for Summit’s ivonescimab cites China-heavy data beyond survival miss
Emerging Trends in National Artificial Intelligence Governance for Health: A Multi-Country Comparative Analysis.
desc: [Health care science] Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping health systems worldwide, offering unprecedented opportunities but also introducing new risks. Effective governance is therefore essential to ensure that AI in health is safe, trustworthy, and aligned with public interest. This article examines emerging global t`rends in AI governance in health across a diverse set of countries. Three major trends are shaping the global governance landscape. First, national health data resources are increasingly treated as strategic assets, reflecting a shift toward digital sovereignty. Countries are investing in nationally governed health data infrastructures to enable AI development while safeguarding national interests. Second, regulators are coordinating between general AI laws and health-specific regulations, adopting different governance approaches based on the countries' situations. Third, regulatory systems are transitioning from static, pre-market gatekeeping to lifecycle-based oversight. Countries such as the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Singapore, and China are pioneering mechanisms to manage adaptive AI systems. Beyond these, emerging themes-including regulatory sandboxes, evolving definitions of AI safety, and the prioritization of equity and digital inclusion-are reshaping national strategies. The analysis highlights the need for interoperable standards, robust data governance, and capacity-building for regulators and health institutions.

title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
desc: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on medical question answering and diagnostic reasoning benchmarks. However, existing evaluations typically provide all patient information upfront and assess only the final diagnosis or rationale. This setup ignores the need to acquire diagnostic evidence incrementally from incomplete information in real-world diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we introduce DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can reconstruct the documented diagnostic trajectory through interactive information seeking. Each benchmark instance is built from a PubMed Central case report and includes an initial presentation, an event bank, a clinical course, and diagnostic references. DiagTrace contains 510 cases across eight specialties, with 225 used to evaluate four LLMs on clinical-course alignment, interaction quality, and efficiency. Results reveal trade-offs in coverage, source-consistent ordering, and turn use.

title: When artificial intelligence falls short: Multimodal analysis improves head and neck lymphoma classification.
desc: [iScience] Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in digital pathology, yet its generalizability in routine diagnostic settings remains challenging. We developed a multimodal framework for classifying head and neck lymphoid lesions using 610 cases from ten institutions. UNI was used for histological feature extraction, while CellViT++ enabled nuclear segmentation and quantitative morphometry, subsequently integrated with clinicopathological variables. The UNI-based model showed limited generalization (accuracy of 0.66, F1 score of 0.65, and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.66), whereas multimodal integration substantially improved internal performance (accuracy of 0.91, F1 score of 0.91, and AUROC of 0.87) and maintained performance across two external cohorts (accuracy of 0.84 and 0.79 and AUROC of 0.84 and 0.80). Class-stratified SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed distinct feature attribution patterns across diagnostic groups, with nuclear morphometric features contributing prominently to model predictions. Morphology alone imposes a clear performance ceiling in head and neck lymphomas. Multimodal integration provides a more reliable and clinically relevant approach, supporting diagnostic triage in routine practice.

title: Call-Efficient ICD-10 Code Prediction via Supervised Candidate Generation and Selective LLM Invocation
desc: Automatic assignment of ICD-10 codes from short clinical diagnosis text is a practical medical text classification and normalization task. The task is difficult because diagnosis phrases are short and noisy, the ICD-10 label space is hierarchical, and the class distribution is strongly imbalanced. This paper presents a call-efficient ICD-10 code prediction pipeline that combines transformer embeddings, tree-based supervised candidate generation, candidate-level reranking, and a gated LLM assistance. The evaluation uses a leakage-safe validation protocol: model and threshold selection are based on out-of-fold cross-validation predictions, while final reporting is performed on a locked test set with no shared source-file groups. The supervised conditional parent-code candidate generator reaches 74.32% Top-1 accuracy on the locked test set and 93.05% Top-10 candidate coverage. A direct zero-shot GPT-5.6-Sol baseline reaches 81.01% Top-1 accuracy, but requires an invocation of this large model for every diagnosis. The final deployable system, Pre-LLM fusion, reaches 81.24% OOF-CV accuracy and 83.19% locked-test accuracy while calling the LLM for only 31.97% of cases. This improves the locked-test error rate from 25.68% for the supervised parent-code baseline to 16.81%, corresponding to a 34.5% relative error reduction. The results show that the most effective role of the LLM is controlled reranking on uncertain examples rather than unrestricted coding or full-dataset invocation.

title: Spatialize before pruning: Multimodal large language model sparsification with supportive tokens.
source: PubMed · Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
desc: [Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society] Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved significant success in integrating vision and language, while they incur substantial computational and memory overhead by processing a vast number of visual tokens. Existing visual token pruning methods disregard the inherent spatial structure of the image, leading to position bias and the erroneous removal of critical visual information. To this end, we introduce SpatialPrune, a novel training-free framework designed to address this challenge and enhance inference efficiency. Our approach directly mitigates this bias by employing a spatial selection mechanism that preserves the native spatial position of visual tokens during pruning. This ensures that token selection is guided by content rather than sequence order. Besides, we present a supportive token compression strategy that identifies valuable information within the pruned set. This strategy efficiently compresses and reintegrates pruned tokens into subsequent layers to minimize overall information loss. Extensive experimental results show that SpatialPrune consistently outperforms competing methods, even with an aggressive 66.7% reduction in visual tokens while maintaining 98.8% of the model's original performance. Our source code will be released at https://github.com/lmd1234/Spatialprune.

title: SimAI: Mechanistic User Simulation through Psychological Network Models
desc: Realistic user simulation enables the study of human interactions when direct experimentation is costly or potentially harmful. However, existing simulators largely overlook the psychological mechanisms that drive user behavior. We introduce SimAI, a framework for mechanistic user simulation that models how psychological factors interact to shape user responses. To overcome the challenge of supervising open-ended behavior, we propose a graph reconstruction objective that provides graph-level rewards based on how well simulated conversations reflect the underlying psychological relationships. To support this approach, we construct PSYCHE, a dataset of 18,576 profile-network pairs derived from 516 psychotherapy cases. Automatic evaluations show that SimAI achieves greater simulation and behavioral diversity than existing patient simulators while maintaining strong profile alignment. In an interactive study with 30 mental-health professionals and trainees, SimAI receives the highest average ratings for conversational authenticity, realistic help-seeking behavior, and clinical training utility. Beyond simulation quality, SimAI enables realistic clinical training and uncovers safety failures in prolonged AI interactions with vulnerable users. Code is available at https://github.com/behavioral-data/ANGEL-UserSim.

title: A Large Language Model Content Analysis of a National Plastic Surgery Residency Advice Library.
source: PubMed · The Journal of surgical research
desc: [The Journal of surgical research] Integrated plastic surgery is a small, competitive field in which guidance travels through mentors and home programs, and published evidence comes largely from program-director surveys. The American Council of Educators in Plastic Surgery maintains a free library of recorded application-advice sessions that has not previously been systematically quantified. Eligible sessions published between April 2020 and July 2026 were transcribed, and speaker roles were identified. Recommendations were extracted and coded for topic, advice pattern, actionability, and resource requirements using Claude Opus 5. A stratified 250-sentence sample was coded by two investigators. The actionability rule was revised after an audit and all units were recoded by the model, the human comparison used labels from the original rule. Seventy-four of 79 sessions provided match advice (63.2 h), yielding 8069 model-extracted recommendations; 70.5% were actionable. Actionability among advice sentences identified by the two human coders was 48.6%-63.4%, a descriptive sample range rather than a corrected corpus estimate. Actionable advice was more likely to be detected, which may increase its proportion in the model-extracted set. Personal-statement guidance emphasized self-presentation, general-strategy guidance emotional well-being, and mentorship guidance advocacy. Resource requirements affected 12.4% of recommendations. At the precondition-instance level, 722 assumptions of access versus 106 alternatives yielded a ratio of 6.8:1 (95% confidence interval, 5.60-8.76). The American Council of Educators in Plastic Surgery library covers multiple stages of the application process and includes advice that depends on resources applicants may not have. Guidance within this library should offer practical alternatives when recommended strategies require mentorship, money, or home-program access.

title: Flexible Multi-Stack Super-Resolution of Clinical Brain MRI Using Hetero-Orientation Variational Encoding: Expert Reader Evaluation in a Nigerian Cohort
desc: High-resolution brain MRI is important for neuroradiological assessment, yet routine clinical protocols often rely on fast, anisotropic 2D acquisitions, particularly in resource-constrained settings. These acquisitions may differ in orientation, alignment and anatomical coverage, resulting in partially overlapping image stacks. Existing learning-based super-resolution methods typically rely on single, under-constrained inputs or fixed multi-stack configurations with idealised acquisition geometry. We introduce MS-HVED, a sequence-agnostic framework for flexible multi-stack brain MRI super-resolution. Available axial, coronal and sagittal stacks are independently encoded into multi-scale Gaussian posteriors and fused using a field-of-view-aware Product-of-Gaussians formulation that limits contributions from unsupported regions. Physics-informed domain randomisation simulates heterogeneous clinical acquisition conditions, including obliqueness, partial coverage and imaging artefacts. MS-HVED achieved competitive or superior reconstruction fidelity across synthetic benchmarks and improved downstream tissue segmentation relative to low-resolution inputs. To assess generalisation beyond the training cohorts, we performed external clinical validation on 30 routine brain MRI examinations from a Nigerian cohort, representing an under-represented population in medical imaging research. These examinations formed the largest component of a blinded reader study involving 44 real cases and seven expert neuroradiologists. In the Nigerian cohort, MS-HVED was preferred over the supervised baseline for overall image quality in 187 of 210 paired assessments. Across all clinical cohorts, MS-HVED achieved higher overall-quality scores with all available inputs (5.93 vs. 4.49, p<.001), with the preference persisting when axial or coronal inputs were omitted (p<.001). Code at github.com/cai4cai/ms-hved

title: Ontology pre-training improves machine learning-based predictions for metabolites.
desc: [PLoS computational biology] Deep learning has recently led to multiple breakthroughs in longstanding biological problems. Recent advances have shown that integration of expert knowledge can improve deep learning model predictive performance in complex domains such as biology. Bio-ontologies offer a rich source of curated biological knowledge that can be harnessed to this end. Here, we describe an intuitive and generalisable approach to embed the knowledge contained in a classification hierarchy derived from a bio-ontology into a deep learning model as an intermediate training step between general-purpose pre-training and task-specific fine-tuning: a process that we call'ontology pre-training'. We show that this approach leads to an improvement in predictive performance and a reduction in training time for a broad range of prediction tasks related to metabolite functions, activities and properties in living systems, using a range of datasets derived from MoleculeNet. We see the biggest improvement for regression tasks, e.g., prediction of lipophilicity and aqueous solubility of molecules, and a robust improvement for most classification tasks. Our approach can be adapted for a wide range of knowledge sources, models and prediction tasks.

title: FM-Recon: Exploring Foundation Model Features for Accelerated Cardiac Cine MRI Reconstruction
desc: Foundation models have demonstrated strong feature extraction capabilities across various medical imaging tasks, yet their potential for MRI reconstruction remains largely unexplored, particularly within unrolled reconstruction networks and under artifact-corrupted inputs. In this work, we explore whether and how features from pretrained foundation models can benefit accelerated cardiac cine MRI reconstruction. To this end, we propose FM-Recon, a framework that refines and integrates extracted features from frozen image encoder of foundation models into an unrolled reconstruction network. Through extensive experiments on the CMRxRecon2023 dataset, we systematically evaluate foundation model features across different reconstruction settings. Our results show that foundation models can extract informative representations from artifact-corrupted inputs and improve reconstruction performance, particularly at moderate acceleration factors. These findings demonstrate the potential of foundation model features for accelerated MRI reconstruction and provide insights into their effective integration into unrolled reconstruction networks.

title: A deep learning-based linear system for liver station in EUS (with video).
desc: [Endoscopic ultrasound] With the widespread adoption of endoscopic techniques, the integration of EUS into hepatology has become an inevitable trend. This study aimed to develop a system that can conduct a comprehensive inspection of liver segments through scanning imaging at 8 stations. A standardized EUS examination protocol for the liver comprises 8 stations. We developed a deep learning-based station classification model using a dataset of 9403 EUS liver images. Internal validation was performed on 2780 EUS images and 26 EUS video clips. To further evaluate the model's clinical utility, a human-machine competition involving 340 liver images was conducted. The same set of 26 video clips in internal video validation was also employed for a crossover study to evaluate the system's effectiveness in reducing the difficulty of interpreting liver EUS images. For station classification, the model achieved an accuracy of 92.52% on image validation and a per-frame accuracy of 85.98% on video validation. In the human-machine comparison, the overall classification accuracy reached 88.53%, which was comparable to the average accuracy of the EUS experts (84.56%, P = 0.064). In the crossover study, trainees' station recognition accuracy improved significantly, with an increase of 16.36% (95% confidence interval, 11.43%-21.29%; P < 0.05). The system demonstrates high accuracy in liver station localization and achieves a classification performance comparable to EUS experts. It shows promise for facilitating standardized hepatic EUS examinations and may contribute to shortening the learning curve for trainees in the future.

title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
desc: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving. We analyze 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, tracing trends over a broad spectrum of lexical, structural, epistemological, and social dimensions. Aside from frequency shifts in some words, most pre-2023 trends continued with limited detectable breaks. Among the notable exceptions, growth in computer science coauthor teams accelerated significantly in Asia, while apparent declines in biomedical topic diversity largely reflected standardization in article formats. Our study establishes an empirical foundation for monitoring the health of global science as LLM adoption deepens.

title: Coarse-to-fine-grained insulator defect detection using two-stage deep learning framework.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] In power transmission and power distribution systems, insulators are the fundamental components which provide mechanical support and electrical isolation between conductors and supporting towers. However, these insulators are continuously exposed to extreme weather conditions, mechanical stress, pollution and dust, which can lead to surface damage and abnormal operation. Conventionally, manual on-site inspection is performed to identify faulty insulators. However, this method is labor intensive, risky, and reactive. With the advancement in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology and deep learning method, automatic visual inspection has replaced the conventional methods. However, automatic visual inspection from UAV images is challenging task due to complex background and small size of the insulators. To address these challenges, we proposed a framework that consists of two stages. In the first stage, you only look once (YOLO)-based is used for extracting candidate region of insulator to get coarse class prediction. During the second stage, the candidate regions are then cropped from the image into image patches and fed to a lightweight patch-level classifier. In order to enhance inter-class separability, hard-pair contrastive classification loss is proposed by adding hard-pair contrastive term to the cross-entropy loss in the embedding space. The proposed technique is evaluated using an open-source insulator defect image dataset. The experiment results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework compared with the YOLO variants and representative two-stage detectors.

title: LeViT-UNet++: Towards Balanced Fine-Grained Details and Context for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
desc: Efficient medical image segmentation is essential for clinical applications requiring fast and accurate delineation, such as surgical navigation, radiation therapy, and real-time image-guided intervention. Despite substantial advances in convolutional neural networks and Transformers, attaining high accuracy under limited computational resources remains difficult, because reducing model complexity often sacrifices fine-grained structural details and global context modeling, yielding an unfavorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. To address this, we propose LeViT-UNet++, an efficient encoder-decoder architecture that better balances local detail preservation and global context modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Haar Wavelet Multi-Scale Downsampling (HWMD) module that decomposes feature representations into low- and high-frequency components to extract multi-scale structural information, thereby mitigating detail loss during downsampling. We further develop a depthwise convolution-based decoder that integrates multi-scale global representations from Transformer blocks with local spatial features, enabling progressive feature refinement while reducing computational overhead. Evaluated on four benchmarks (Synapse, ACDC, LA2018, and MSD Heart) under both 2D and 3D settings, LeViT-UNet++ achieves competitive accuracy with a compact parameter footprint and fast inference. On Synapse, for instance, it attains a DSC of 76.57% with only 8.025M parameters and 241.72 FPS, confirming a favorable accuracy-efficiency balance. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining wavelet-based multi-scale feature extraction with lightweight local-global feature fusion for efficient medical segmentation. The source code is available at https://github.com/apple1986/levit_unet_pp.

title: Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE.
desc: [Frontiers in sociology] Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18-35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p < 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = -0.106; all p < 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p < 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

title: HealthCLBench:Evaluating Context Learning in Health Conversations through Controlled Case Clusters
desc: Complex health conversations require answers grounded in individual information and currently valid evidence. We evaluate health context learning: acquiring, integrating, and applying relevant context during inference with fixed model parameters to answer health questions and respond appropriately to changes in facts, evidence, or task goals. To our knowledge, Chinese-language medical benchmarks have yet to systematically combine explicit contextual difficulties, controlled case variations, and member-specific medical criteria for open-ended answers. We introduce HealthCLBench, comprising 328 controlled clusters, 1,103 cases, and 4,931 rubric criteria across medical consultation and everyday health management. Members share backgrounds while evidence, patient states, or task goals change; each has its own medical scoring requirements. A 70-person medical team annotates and reviews the simulated cases and their rubrics. Human review of 700 full-context responses from the original evaluation yields 90.5% pooled agreement with the original automated judgments at the rubric-item level. We report full-context and query-only results for seven general-purpose models and Ant Afu. Across the eight systems, full- query differences range from 11.83 to 31.76 case points and from 10.87 to 38.97 geometric cluster points. GPT-6-Astra leads both full-context metrics at 75.03 and 60.42, followed by Claude-Opus-5-5 and Ant Afu. Cross-condition differences describe score changes under the reported evaluation settings. Response comparisons reveal failures in checking historical information, expressing uncertainty when warranted, and ensuring recommendations respect required conditions. The resource supports model comparison and targeted follow-up evaluation.

title: Commercially available multimodal LLMs for EEG-based prognostication after cardiac arrest.
desc: [Resuscitation] Machine-learning and deep-learning approaches have been successfully applied to EEG-based prognostication in comatose patients after cardiac arrest (CA), but typically rely on task-specific signal processing, feature extraction, and model development. Here, we investigated whether two commercially available multimodal large language models (LLMs) could predict neurological outcome directly from EEG images. Thirty-three comatose patients on the first day after CA from a prospective cohort were included. For each patient, a single 10-second EEG segment displayed using a longitudinal bipolar montage was rendered as PNG image. ChatGPT 5.4. and Claude Opus 4.7 were instructed to estimate the probability for favorable outcome for each case based on the EEG and a generic information block describing conditions of recordings. Five different prompting strategies were used, including few-shot prompting where four exemplary EEGs (not from the 33 patients) were provided. Predictive performance was quantified using AUC and accuracy. Across prompting strategies, the AUC ranged from 0.86 to 0.99 for ChatGPT and from 0.74 to 1.00 for Claude. The highest accuracy achieved by both models was 93.9% using few-shot prompting. As reference, a previously published dedicated deep-learning model achieved 100% on the same cohort. In this exploratory study of a small cohort, multimodal LLMs showed variable but potentially promising discrimination for predicting favorable outcome from single EEG image in comatose patients after CA. Performance depended substantially on prompt design. These findings require confirmation in a larger cohort.

title: Anticipating or Speculating? Making Futures Pay in AI Ethics
desc: Philosophers have recently been trying to develop uniform decision rules for instances in which physicians' judgments diverge from the recommendations of medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems. I argue that this effort is fatally flawed because the performance and appropriate use of algorithmic recommendation systems by physicians are highly context-specific, empirical medical matters rather than epistemological ones. In such instances, general decision rules can be stipulated only to the extent that they abstract away from relevant, indeed determinative, contextual circumstances. The alleged problem of physician-AI disagreement, and others like it, play into longstanding disputes in technology ethics about the viability and utility of envisioning possible futures: is this useful "anticipation" or wasteful "speculation"? I suggest that the two may be distinguished. Anticipation explores plausible futures to help inform present actions under irreducible uncertainty. Speculation abstracts away uncertainty, developing formal solutions to stipulated circumstances whose relationship to the real present is often quite unclear. Efforts to develop crisp philosophical solutions to physician-AI disagreement, among other problems, fall into the latter category. Technology ethics should remember that fruitful futures thinking must both begin from and return to the messy, uncertain present.

title: From Watts-Strogatz to deep learning: Small-world topology and modular organization in pruned neural networks.
source: PubMed · Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
desc: [Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society] Despite neural network pruning's success in removing up to 90% of parameters, the theoretical basis for favorable sparsity regimes remains poorly understood. We establish a mathematical framework connecting small-world network theory to pruned neural network topology. Through analysis of ResNet and Vision Transformer architectures on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-100, we demonstrate that convolutional networks exhibit small-world properties (σSW = 2.0) with high modularity (Q = 0.68) when pruned to moderate connection density (8-12%, Pareto-optimal point ∼ 11%)-coinciding with the phase transition threshold in Watts-Strogatz graphs-while Transformers show minimal modularity due to global self-attention. We derive that modularity follows exponential decay with density under assumptions of random inter-community edge addition and validate this relationship across architectures. Interventional experiments with enforced topological constraints demonstrate that small-world structure correlates with improved performance at 10% density, though causal mechanisms require further investigation. Our results provide theoretical motivation for empirically observed pruning ratios and explain architectural differences in learned representations.

title: A Visual Information Extraction System Using Multimodal Large Language Models for Scanned Cognitive and Behavioral Assessments
desc: Objective. Paper-based assessments are common in patient care, but handwriting and scanning artifacts make these forms difficult to process at scale. This study proposes a modular, multimodal LLM-based system with human oversight for extracting fields and scores. We conducted a qualitative analysis of the use of LLMs for hand-drawing analysis. Materials and Methods. The system processes cognitive assessments (i.e., MMSE, MoCA, Mini-Cog) and the NICHQ Vanderbilt Assessment using two modules: 1) a form classifier that assigns a scanned page to a form type, followed by a corresponding 2) score extractor that extracts fields and scores into a schema. A human-in-the-loop design utilizing dual-model validation engages human annotators when two LLMs disagree, limiting manual review to challenging pages only. Results. End-to-end accuracy for cognitive assessments was 88%, with most form types exceeding 90%. For the NICHQ Vanderbilt, overall accuracy reached 97.5%, with all form types above 96%. The human-in-the-loop design further improved cognitive assessment accuracy to 97.5% while reducing manual work by 63.8%. In the Mini-Cog Clock Drawing task, qualitative analysis showed that 62.3% of all extraction errors stemmed from ambiguous drawing, in which cases the LLM provided reasonable readings. Discussion. Compared to current manual data extraction, our LLM-based system reduces processing time by 10 to 20 times and costs by over 12 times. The modular design allows seamless expansion to additional form types. Conclusion. Our system provides an accurate, scalable, and cost-efficient solution for structuring data trapped in handwritten paper forms for clinical decision support.

title: Generative AI dependency and perceived learning outcomes among university students: an indirect association involving effort regulation.
desc: [Frontiers in psychology] Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into university learning, raising questions about dependency-oriented reliance and self-regulation. Drawing on a self-regulated learning perspective, this study examined associations among GenAI dependency, effort regulation, and multidimensional perceived learning outcomes, including the statistical indirect association involving effort regulation. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 982 students at three higher education institutions in Guangdong Province, China. Confirmatory factor analysis and covariance-based structural equation modeling were conducted, with indirect associations tested using 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for GenAI use frequency. The measurement model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.953, TLI = 0.944, RMSEA = 0.043, SRMR = 0.041). GenAI dependency showed a small negative total association with perceived learning outcomes (β = -0.087) and was negatively associated with effort regulation (β = -0.257). Effort regulation was positively associated with perceived learning outcomes (β = 0.497). The residual direct association was nonsignificant (β = 0.041), whereas the indirect association was negative and significant (β = -0.128). After adjustment for GenAI use frequency, the indirect association remained significant, but the small total association was no longer significant. The findings highlight effort regulation as a relevant learner-controlled process in the association between GenAI dependency and perceived learning outcomes. They also distinguish dependency-oriented reliance from frequency of GenAI use. The cross-sectional design and potential classroom clustering warrant cautious interpretation.

title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
desc: Background: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer an alternative to encoder-based clinical named entity recognition (NER), but their performance on fine-grained Japanese extraction tasks and sensitivity to generation settings remain uncertain. Methods: We compared two fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines with nine open-weight LLMs on iCorpus, which defines 113 entity categories. The evaluation used 433 sentences from 36 test documents; 1,672 sentences were used for training. LLMs were evaluated using zero-shot prompting with and without JSON Schema constraints and three-seed QLoRA fine-tuning. Fine-tuned models were assessed under different output-token limits, including 900 and larger model-specific limits of 2,600 or 4,096 tokens. Performance was measured using sentence-level label-surface matching with relaxed and exact-surface F1. Results: The highest zero-shot relaxed F1 was 0.337, compared with 0.836-0.841 for the BERT baselines. At the larger output limits, all eight fine-tuned LLMs with at least 13B total parameters exceeded both BERT baselines (relaxed F1, 0.882-0.914; exact-surface F1, 0.840-0.880). Across three-seed means, increasing the output limit improved relaxed F1 by 0.052-0.085, alongside higher recall and fewer length-limited outputs. JSON Schema constraints changed relaxed F1 by -0.014 to +0.008 among seven models outside the two reasoning-oriented configurations, while medical-general model pairs showed no consistent advantage for medical specialization. Conclusions: On this historical Japanese case-report benchmark, task-specific fine-tuning combined with adequate generation capacity was associated with stronger LLM extraction performance. Output-token limits materially affected comparisons with BERT, whereas enforcing output structure alone did not overcome low zero-shot accuracy.

title: A deep learning model for flood forecasting based on dynamic lag encoding and multi-head attention.
desc: [iScience] Conventional flood forecasting models often struggle to effectively capture the time-lag characteristics of rainfall-runoff responses within a basin, and their decision-making processes generally lack interpretability. This study used 19 years (1979-1997) of multi-station rainfall and outlet discharge data from the Hydrological Yearbook of the Yellow River Basin, and selected 53 representative flood events from the Huangfuchuan Basin for model development and evaluation. A deep learning flood forecasting model (D-TMA-LSTM) was developed by integrating dynamic lag encoding with a multi-head attention mechanism. The results show that D-TMA-LSTM outperformed the original LSTM and D-LSTM across forecast lead times from t+1 to t+6. At t+1, NSE, KGE, and R2 values were 0.959, 0.934, and 0.964, respectively, while RMSE decreased by 31.74%. The model also maintained stable performance at t+6, providing an effective framework for flood forecasting in basins with complex rainfall-runoff lag responses.

title: Not All Evidence Is Admissible: Evidence Governance for Tool-Augmented Medical Agents
desc: Tool-augmented medical agents treat whatever their tools return as evidence. We show that this default is costly: medical tools fail silently, and a frozen reasoner cannot ignore what enters its context, so many cases it would have answered correctly are flipped to wrong once tool outputs are added. We call this evidence hijacking. $\mathcal{V}$-information explains the phenomenon: the reasoner has lost the option to ignore, so a tool output can carry negative usable information, and moving the decision of what to keep outside the reasoner restores that option. The theory further shows that part of any filtering gain comes merely from letting the reasoner see less, and only selection by content lets it see better. Building on this, we recast tool-augmented reasoning as evidence governance, which separates deciding what counts as evidence from the reasoner that answers, and propose context-independent evidence governance (CIEG), the first medical agent framework that rules, after acquisition, on whether each individual tool output may enter as evidence. Every tool output is written as a card that can be checked against the raw input; an independent checker that sees only the input and the cards decides which cards become evidence; and the reasoner answers from the admitted cards alone, with no training anywhere. On medical question answering, fundus glaucoma screening, and chest X-ray pneumonia classification, it achieves the highest accuracy among models of comparable scale, and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art tool-using agents and multi-agent systems built on the same backbone at lower cost.

title: Teachers' basic psychological need satisfactions and their intentions to use generative artificial intelligence: the mediating role of engagement in professional development.
desc: [Frontiers in psychology] Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new opportunities for instructional innovation, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying teachers' intentions to adopt it remain unclear.
